KITCHEN LESSON · KITCHEN THINGS · AGES 3–6 YEARS

Ladle — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the ladle in two sittings: the cold practice where pouring is free, then the real serving where the child feeds the family and earns the thank-yous.

What is this?

A ladle is the long-handled deep spoon that scoops soup from pot to bowl — and the tool that puts a child in the host’s seat at dinner.

What does it mean?

Ladling is a full command course: dip depth, fill control, steady carry, targeted pour. It is also the job that earns thank-yous — and thank-yous are fuel.

What does the child need to know?

You need the ladle, cold soup or water for the sink practice, and the four-word sequence: dip… fill… carry… pour. Warm-not-hot soup is the promotion.

Why this matters

Serving others is the rare chore that comes with applause built in. Every bowl served lands a "thank you" — and a child with thanks coming keeps ladling.

What it teaches

Dip-and-fill control, steady carrying (the walk matters), targeted pouring, counting servings, and host pride.

Words to learn

ladlescoopdippourservethank you

Say this to your child

“"Ladle! The big deep spoon. Dip in the soup… fill it up… carry it steady… POUR — one bowl, served! Now everyone: dip, fill, pour! One for daddy, one for grandma… and one for YOU. Thank you, chef!"”

Step by step

  1. Meet the deep spoon: "ladle! The soup scooper — see the deep bowl on the handle?"
  2. Sink practice with cold soup: "dip… fill… carry… POUR into the bowl. No drips — steady hands!"
  3. Repeat until the pour is confident: bowls lined up, one fill per bowl.
  4. The promotion: warm (not hot) soup at dinner — the child ladles each bowl, counting: "one for daddy… one for grandma… one for ME!"
  5. The applause: thank-yos collected, the ladle washed and hung by its newest expert.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "ladle" sits over a green-handled ladle, its deep bowl up — ready for the dip that starts every serve.

Ask your child

"What does the ladle do?" (scoops and serves) "Show me dip… fill… pour!" "Who got your soup tonight?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might serve every meal, count the bowls aloud, or ladle the bath toys (transfer of skills) — the host, seated.

Out in the real world

Ladles work every soup pot, punch bowl and stew night. Each one is a hiring opportunity: "a ladle — the serving job is yours!"

Try it together

Soup Kitchen: bowls for every teddy, one ladle, cold water "soup" — fill each order, count the customers. Service with a smile, math with a ladle.

Understanding check

Ask: "What does the ladle do?" (serves soup) "What are the four words?" (dip, fill, carry, pour) "Who says thank you?" (everyone!)

This lesson pairs with the Ladle flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Kitchen Things.
